verses.1: Therefore, casting away all malice and deceit, and hypocrisy, and envy, and all evil speaking,
verses.2: like newborn infants, long for the pure, rational milk of the word, so that in it you may grow for salvation,
verses.3: if you have tasted that the Lord is good.
verses.4: To him you are drawing near, a living stone, rejected by people but chosen and precious in the sight of God.
verses.5: And you yourselves, as living stones, are being built up as a spiritual house, a holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
verses.6: For it is in the scripture: "Behold, I lay in Zion a stone, a cornerstone chosen and precious; and the one who believes in him will not be put to shame."
verses.7: So for you who believe, this is honor; but for those who disbelieve, the stone which they rejected has become the head of the corner,
verses.8: and a stone of stumbling, and a rock of offense. They stumble because they disobey the word, as they were destined to do.
verses.9: But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for his own possession, in order to proclaim the excellencies of the one who called you out of darkness into his wonderful light.
verses.10: Once you were not a people, but now you are God's people; once you had not received mercy, but now you have received mercy.
verses.11: Beloved, I urge you as sojourners and exiles to keep away from the desires of the flesh, which wage war against the soul,
verses.12: having your behavior among the nations honorable, so that when they speak against you as evildoers, they may see your good deeds and glorify God on the day of visitation.
verses.13: Be subject to every human institution for the Lord's sake, whether to the king as supreme,
verses.14: or to governors as sent by him to punish evildoers and to praise those who do good.
verses.15: For this is the will of God, that by doing good you may silence the ignorance of foolish people.
verses.16: Live as free people, but do not use your freedom as a cover for evil; live as God's slaves.
verses.17: Honor everyone, love the family of believers, fear God, honor the king.
verses.18: Servants, be subject to your masters in everything, with fear and trembling, not only to those who are kind and gentle but also to those who are unreasonable.
verses.19: For this is a pleasing thing, if someone bears up under suffering while enduring unjustly, because of a conscience toward God.
verses.20: For what credit is it if you sin and are beaten for it? But if you endure when you suffer for doing good, that is grace from God.
verses.21: For to this you were called, because Christ also suffered for you, leaving you an example, so that you might follow in his footsteps.
verses.22: He did no sin, nor was any deceit found in his mouth.
verses.23: When he was reviled, he did not revile in return; when he suffered, he did not threaten, but entrusted himself to the one who judges justly.
verses.24: He himself bore our sins in his body on the cross, so that we, having died to sins, might live for righteousness. By his wounds you have been healed.
verses.25: For you were like sheep going astray, but now you have returned to the shepherd and overseer of your souls.

notes:
Notes
- v. 1: "rational milk of the word" reflects the Greek "λογικὸν ἄδολον γάλα" — "rational" is taken to mean "understanding" or "spiritual nourishment through reason."
- v. 5: "spiritual sacrifices" is a standard interpretation of "πνευματικὰς θυσίας," referring to acts of worship and service.
- v. 7: "head of the corner" is a rendering of "κεφαλὴν γωνίας," which is the Greek equivalent of the Hebrew "kephal keren," or "chief cornerstone."
- v. 9: "royal priesthood" is a direct rendering of "βασίλειον ἱεράτευμα," reflecting the unique role of believers in the new covenant.
- v. 24: "by his wounds you have been healed" is a direct translation of "οὗ τῷ μώλωπι ἰάθητε," which uses the metaphor of healing through Christ’s suffering.
